{"checked_at":"2026-10-05T01:02:29.004Z","mailbox":"recipient mailbox (separate account)","gmail_id":"1a1099506ce56fbb","labelIds":["UNREAD","IMPORTANT","CATEGORY_PERSONAL","INBOX"],"to":"renter@recipient-test.example","subject":"Your new service page: Tree Removal in Spokane","date":"Mon, 5 Oct 2026 03:02:03 +0200","in_inbox":true,"body_chars":5630,"html_list_items":7,"body":"Title tag: Tree Removal Spokane | Prairie Line Tree Removal
Meta description: Tree removal in Spokane for tall pines and dead trees
near your house, garage or fence. Wood hauled away or left as rounds. Free
on-site quotes.
Tree Removal in Spokane

Prairie Line Tree Removal connects Spokane homeowners with a local tree
crew for whole-tree removal. Most calls come from people with a tall pine
or a dead tree standing close to the house, garage or fence.

The crew serves North Spokane, Five Mile Prairie, Mead, Nine Mile Falls and
South Hill. Quotes are free and given after the crew looks at the tree in
person.
What our Spokane tree removal service covers

We remove whole trees. The crew cuts up the tree and hauls away the
branches and trunk wood. If you want to keep the wood, tell us when you ask
for the quote and the trunk is cut into rounds and left on site for you.

Stump grinding is available as an add-on and is quoted separately from the
removal.
Pine tree removal near a house, garage or fence

Some lots have tall pines growing close to the house, garage or fence. When
there is no room to fell a tree, the crew can take it down in sections by
climbing. Whether that applies to your tree is decided at the on-site look,
once the crew sees what is around it.

For pine tree removal in Spokane, the most useful thing you can do is point
out exactly what the tree stands next to, so the quote reflects the real
job.
Dead tree removal

A dead tree close to a structure is worth getting looked at. A dead or
damaged tree can call for a different approach than a healthy one, so the
crew assesses it in person before settling on a plan and a price.

You do not need to figure out how to take it down. Describe where it stands
and what it is near, and the crew handles the rest of the assessment.
Alley and side-yard access

Some lots are reached from an alley, and some have narrow side yards. When
the gate is too narrow for equipment, the crew carries branches and wood
out by hand.

Tell us about the gate width and the route from the tree to the street or
alley. It helps the crew plan the cleanup as well as the removal.
Stump grinding in Spokane

If you want the stump gone too, ask for stump grinding in Spokane when you
request your quote. It is priced as its own line, so you can decide whether
to add it once you have seen the number.

Grinding takes the stump down; filling the hole with topsoil or seed is not
part of the service.
Get your quote request ready

You do not need to be home for the quote if the tree can be seen from the
street or the yard is open. These details help the crew give you a useful
answer:

   - Where the tree stands relative to the house, garage, fence or alley
   - Whether the tree is a pine, and whether it looks dead or damaged
   - Gate width and whether the side yard is narrow
   - Whether you want to keep the wood as rounds or have it all hauled away
   - Whether you want the stump ground
   - Whether the tree is on your property or near a road or alley
   - The best way to reach you: call or text (509) 555-0142, or use the
   quote form

What is not included

This service does not include trimming or pruning trees that stay, filling
the stump hole with topsoil or seed, or splitting firewood. We also cannot
work on any tree in contact with power lines.

If a service wire from the pole to your house runs near the tree and you
are an Avista customer, note that Avista does not prune around that wire.
You can request a no-cost service drop at (800) 227-9187, which
de-energizes and temporarily removes the line so the work can be done
safely. It is available Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., and must be
requested at least three business days in advance, so book it before the
removal date (details on myavista.com, tree trimming FAQ).

On permits: in the City of Spokane, a tree on private property needs no
city permit. Removing a tree in the public right-of-way needs an Urban
Forestry permit, and the right-of-way width varies from street to street.
Check before working on trees near roads or alleys. Urban Forestry can be
reached at 509.363.5495.
Frequently asked questions

*Do I have to be home for the quote?*
No, as long as the tree can be seen from the street or the yard is open.
The crew can look at it without you there. Leave a note about gate access
if there is one.

*How much does tree removal cost in Spokane?*
The price depends on the tree and the access, so the crew gives it after
seeing the tree in person. The quote is free.

*Can I keep the wood?*
Yes. Tell us when you ask for the quote and the trunk wood is cut into
rounds and left on site. Otherwise the branches and wood are hauled away.
Splitting the rounds into firewood is not part of the service.

*Is stump grinding included?*
It is quoted separately as an add-on. Say you want it when you request your
quote and it will be priced alongside the removal.

*Do I need a permit to remove a tree at my house?*
Not for a tree on private property in the City of Spokane. If the tree may
stand in the public right-of-way near a road or alley, call Urban Forestry
at 509.363.5495 before you book the removal.

*How do I ask for a quote?*
Call or text (509) 555-0142, or send the quote form. Calls and forms are
answered on business days.
Book your free on-site quote

Call (509) 555-0142 or send the quote form to book a free on-site quote for
tree removal in North Spokane, Five Mile Prairie, Mead, Nine Mile Falls or
South Hill.
